label: Registration
title: CyberAlchemy Lab × Craft Hackathon — Registration
description:
Build an interface people love to use, or take an ambitious idea further.

Choose one new individual project using Craft and CyberAlchemy Lab, in one of two categories: Studio front-end or Open projects. Participants choose one winner in each category.

Registration: October 16, 2026 at 18:00 to October 23 at 23:59:59.
Project month: October 24, 2026 at 00:00 to November 23 at 23:59:59.
Voting: November 24, 2026 at 12:00 to November 25 at 18:00.
Final results: November 25, 2026 by 23:59:59.

Studio front-end: develop a beautiful, wild CyberAlchemy Lab / Craft Studio interface, with useful new UX features in service of human–machine ergonomics. Open projects: the original ambitious-project challenge remains, with agent companies, worlds, learning systems and your own ideas welcome.

Each category has one US$200 prize: reimbursement for one month of ChatGPT Pro at the US$200 tier. Winners buy their subscription on their own accounts and submit receipts. The cap includes taxes and fees; excess costs and renewals remain theirs.

Free entry, age 18+. One person, one new project, one category. Each registered participant may submit one final ballot with one vote per category, or abstain in either; no self-votes.

This form registers a participant, not a project. Use the same Google Account to register, submit and vote. All times use Brasília time (UTC-3).

Organizer: CyberAlchemy Lab. Questions: hello@cyberalchemize.com.

label: Project submission
title: CyberAlchemy Lab × Craft Hackathon — Project Submission
description:
Show the idea. Show the work.

Submit one new individual project using Craft and CyberAlchemy Lab. Choose exactly one category: Studio front-end or Open projects.

Studio front-end: show a beautiful, wild Studio interface with new UX features that favor human–machine ergonomics. Explain and demonstrate how the interactions help people work with machines. Open projects keeps the original open-ended Craft and Lab challenge.

A working prototype is enough. Include an accessible demo of up to three minutes, access/run instructions, a stable version, credits and known limitations. Identify illustrative or simulated behavior honestly.

Build from October 24, 2026 at 00:00. Submit by November 23, 2026 at 23:59:59 Brasília time (UTC-3). Use the same Google Account as registration. You may edit before the deadline; new features and replacement demos are excluded afterward.

Participants choose one winner per category. Each winner receives reimbursement up to US$200 for one month of ChatGPT Pro at the US$200 tier, against a receipt. See the full rules for fees and delivery.

Questions: hello@cyberalchemize.com.
questions: Use the display name from your registration.
Multiple choice · Required · Exactly one selection
Choose one category for this project. One person may enter only one project in one category.
Give your project a name people can remember.
What does your project do, and who is it for?
Describe the question or problem that inspired it, the intended user, and what the working prototype demonstrates.
Identify the Craft tools, models, or components you used and explain their role in your project. Be specific.
How did you use CyberAlchemy Lab?
Explain which lab concepts, tools, or components your project uses and how they contribute to the result.
Paste a link to your project, repository, or accessible project files. Provide any necessary access instructions below.
A demo of up to three minutes showing the core behavior. Make the video accessible to all participants without paid access.
Identify the exact version shown in your demo: a commit hash, release tag, or dated export.
How can we access or run your project?
Give the steps needed to verify the prototype. Describe setup requirements. Do not submit passwords, API keys, or other secrets.
Credit libraries, starter templates, datasets, images, or other reused material. Describe any AI assistance and what you created yourself. Write “None” if applicable.
State what the prototype does not yet handle, any known issues, and which parts are illustrative or simulated.
New projects created for this hackathon are eligible. Team entries and improvements to an existing project are excluded.
I confirm that this is my new individual project, that it uses both Craft and CyberAlchemy Lab, and that I have credited reused work and followed the hackathon rules.
confirmation:
Your project submission has been received.

label: Participant voting
title: CyberAlchemy Lab × Craft Hackathon — Participant Vote
description:
Choose one project in each category.

Explore the eligible gallery before voting: [PROJECT_GALLERY_URL]

Studio front-end: consider visual beauty and originality, inventive UX features, and demonstrated human–machine ergonomics. Open projects: consider originality, usefulness, the demonstrated prototype and meaningful use of Craft and CyberAlchemy Lab.

Submit one final ballot with one project choice per category, or choose “Abstain” in either category. Do not vote for your own project. A self-vote is invalid in that category; a valid choice in the other category can still count. Submitted ballots cannot be changed.

Only participants on the final roster can vote. Use the same Google Account as registration. Multiple accounts, automated votes, buying votes and vote trading are prohibited.

Voting opens November 24, 2026 at 12:00 and closes November 25 at 18:00. Final results are due November 25 by 23:59:59. All times use Brasília time (UTC-3).

The most-voted eligible project in each category wins that category’s US$200 subscription reimbursement prize. Each category needs at least one valid vote; an unawarded prize does not transfer. Individual choices stay private; validated aggregate category results are published.

Questions or voting reports: hello@cyberalchemize.com.
